reviewerModel: GPT-6 (exact model identifier not exposed to this reviewer)
reviewScope: Read-only source and final-poster critique; no browser, source edits, rebuild, or independent runtime execution. Video comparison uses current Astra transcripts and comparative review evidence, not fresh playback. Acceptance is editorial, not integrated UI QA approval.
rationale: Substantively better than the rejected gatehouses, and a valid coverage interactive, but still below the meaningful spatial-affordance threshold for an optional 3D companion. Independent patch/coverage choices add agency beyond the video; depth and camera inspection add little to the explanation beyond a flat two-lane interactive.

findings.issue: The added value comes from controls, not spatial inspection.
findings.evidence: interaction.js change() independently selects patch and coverage; runProbe() casts a straight ray at fixed nose height against the active wall. build_scene.py fixes both lane positions and supplies only bricked, barrier, or open bays. A top-down blocked/open lane view preserves all four combinations, unprobed VALID, and every outcome without losing a relevant relationship. Orbit reveals architectural surfaces and the far side of the same binary obstruction, not an additional coverage relationship.
findings.recommendation: Omit this 3D candidate; retain the interaction idea if a flat companion is wanted. Raycast implementation is not itself evidence of spatial teaching value.

findings.issue: The revision genuinely resolves the prior interaction objection.
findings.evidence: No lid reveal or sequential stage progression remains. Coverage can be removed and patch choice reversed; the unused probe stays on the rack. Astra already teaches new-test pass/existing-test failure and revised-patch review at 0–28s, while this adds reader-chosen B+new-only comparison. That is a real interactive improvement, but does not by itself justify depth.

findings.issue: The final poster clips the alternative wall and weakens probe identification.
findings.evidence: In the inspected 1200x900 poster, B extends past the right edge; its right pier and cornice are cropped. The valid key is nearly edge-on on its rack. EMPTY and VALID read clearly at native size, but the camera allocates substantial space to parking and architecture. This is current poster evidence, not a claim about responsive browser rendering.
findings.recommendation: If retained despite the editorial verdict, reframe both wall extremes and show the key silhouette clearly before coordinator UI QA.

findings.issue: Faithful as a bounded test-grading metaphor.
findings.evidence: Empty expects stop and valid expects through; failure flags compare observed intersection with those expectations. The both-pass caption explicitly says two probes support review, not release. No repeated trials, general reliability, authentication implementation, or complete coverage is demonstrated. These limits agree with the guide.

limitations: GLB bytes were hashed; Blender build source was inspected, but scene.blend and GLB geometry were not independently loaded.
Author-reported headless harness results were read, not rerun. No browser or alternate-state renders were generated.
